lines.text: Most organisations know how they work.
Very few can answer a question about it in less than a week.
What depends on this system? Who owns this information? What breaks if we change it?
The answers exist, but they are spread across diagrams, spreadsheets, a service desk, an asset register and a few people's memory.
So every question becomes a small project.
The knowledge is locked in pictures, current only until someone redraws them.
The facts are copied in by hand from systems that already hold them.
No team, report or assistant can read it without an export.
And the vocabulary belongs to the tool, not to the business.
The EA Repository keeps the architecture as governed data, not drawings.
Ask a question and the answer comes back in seconds, every fact citing the element it came from.
Facts flow in from the systems that own them, and every row keeps its source.
It runs on the data platform, where people and agents read the same model.
What the model can describe is yours to change: a metamodel, tried on a copy first.
And change stays governed. Anyone can propose, owners review, and a person approves.
The assistant drafts and explains. It never approves.
Here is the application, with the sample model of a fictional university.
The first time you open it, a short welcome says where to start.
The navigation follows the work: discover, contribute, then manage.
Every screen has its help at the top right.
It opens beside the screen: why it exists, what you see, how to use it, and what your role may do.
Browse finds any element by name, type or status.
Open one, and its page shows what it is, where it stands, and what it relates to.
Its views are generated from the model. Nothing is drawn by hand, and every shape is an element you can open.
Ask takes a question in plain words.
Here, the impact of changing a course offering: a view of it, the answer, and every element the answer cites.
Impact lists what depends on an element, and what it depends on, hop by hop.
To change the model, you hand in a design page.
Write it here, with its preview beside it, or drop in files and drawings.
The assistant links what already exists, adopts what is new, and asks about what it cannot settle, such as which work package delivers the change.
You check every row, then apply them to a branch. Main is not touched.
On Branches, the reviewers of each element type approve the change.
Then it is merged into main, row by row.
Target state shows where each element is headed, and the work package that takes it there.
Imports and feeds bring facts in from other systems, and keep a record of every run.
The metamodel is data too: its types, relationships and notation, kept in versions.
A new version is tried in an organisation of its own before it is applied.
Admins give workspace groups their roles.
And Health shows what needs a steward's attention.
To learn more, open the Guide, or press the question mark on any screen.
Agents draft. People approve. And the architecture stays current, cited and shared.
